translationRepairs: They seized the supply train and advanced on Jinan.
They seized the supply train and advanced on Jining.
The source names 濟寧, not 濟南; Jinan is a different city and the replacement restores the correct place.
They plundered the baggage train and pressed forward toward Jinan.
They plundered the baggage train and pressed forward toward Jining.
進薄濟寧 is an advance on Jining; the literal English wrongly substitutes Jinan.
The next day they fought again: the Yan army on the northeast, Yong's army on the southwest; from the seventh to the second hour of the afternoon, victory seesawed.
The next day they fought again: the Yan army on the northeast, Yong's army on the southwest; from the chen hour to the wei hour, victory seesawed.
自辰至未 names the chen and wei double-hours (morning to early afternoon); 'the seventh to the second hour of the afternoon' misreads those labels.
He marched with Chang Yuchun against the Yuan capital and was killed in action.
He marched with Chang Yuchun to take the Yuan capital and was killed in action.
下元都 means taking the Yuan capital, not merely campaigning against it; the replacement matches 下 and the unit's own literal.
Soon after he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.
Soon after he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Military Commission.
行後府 is the Rear Chief Military Commission, not a palace; Palace invents a civil household office the Chinese does not name.
Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.
Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Military Commission.
後府 in 都督僉事 is the rear military commission; Rear Palace is a mistranslation of 府.
In the third month of Yongle 7 the emperor toured Beiping.
In the third month of Yongle 7 the emperor toured Beijing.
The tour destination is 北京, distinct from 北平 in the preceding appointment; Beiping is the wrong toponym here.
In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle the Emperor toured Beiping.
In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle the Emperor toured Beijing.
The Chinese is 北京, not 北平; the literal must follow the named place.
The next year, in the first month, He Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and wiped them out.
The next year, in the first month, He Fu and Commissioner-in-chief Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Fu and Yan, and wiped them out.
鄜 is Fu, not Zhulu, and 都督 is commissioner-in-chief rather than vice commissioner (都督僉事); both replacements restore the source.
In the first month of the following year Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and annihilated them completely.
In the first month of the following year Fu and Commissioner-in-chief Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Fu and Yan, and annihilated them completely.
The same clause has 都督 and 鄜、延; Vice Commissioner and Zhulu are not in the Chinese.
By then the founding emperor was dead and the new emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
By then the founding emperor was dead and the Hui Emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
惠帝 is a specific ruler-name, not a generic new emperor; the replacement restores the omitted designation.
At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huandi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huidi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
惠帝 romanizes as Huidi; Huandi would be 桓帝 and is a naming error.
He betrothed Fu's niece, the Xu clan, as Princess of Zhao.
He betrothed Fu's niece, née Xu, as consort of the Prince of Zhao.
徐氏 marks the niece as née Xu, and 趙王妃 is consort of the Prince of Zhao, not a princess and not 'the Xu clan' as the person.
He marched on Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the Yuan commander and more than twenty officers under him, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.
He marched on Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the enemy commander-in-chief and more than twenty officers under him, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.
元帥 is a military rank; reading it as Yuan dynasty invents a polity the Shu campaign sentence does not name.
The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; he sent Commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to put them down.
The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; he sent Commander Lu Bing and Cheng's son Tong by separate routes to put them down.
成遣…與其子統 makes 其 Cheng's son 統, not Lu Bing's; the English 'his' after Lu Bing misassigns kinship.

Sinzhou Pacification Commissioner Tian Chen and Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Zongding raised troops against one another; an edict ordered Gu Cheng to press their borders with fifty thousand troops, and Chen and the others were captured.

Sizhou Pacification Commissioner Tian Chen and Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Zongding raised troops against one another; an edict ordered Gu Cheng to press their borders with fifty thousand troops, and Chen and the others were captured.
思州 is Sizhou, as in the next sentence's 思州、思南; Sinzhou is a wrong romanization of the same place.
He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
He was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
太傅 is Grand Mentor, distinct from Grand Preceptor 太師.
He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
He was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
